lesson_status_at_scan: missing; writer must place the supplied embeds
assessment: The four briefed visuals are distinct and load-bearing: bin sampling connects the DTFT to the DFT, the basis grid exposes each coefficient as a correlation, the real-spectrum ledger prevents layout and scaling mistakes, and the controlled padding comparison separates denser frequency sampling from a longer observation. All are constructed mathematical explanations; no authenticity-bearing raster is needed.
scope_guardrail: Use the forward convention X[k]=sum_{n=0}^{N-1} x[n] exp(-j2pi kn/N) and inverse x[n]=(1/N)sum_{k=0}^{N-1}X[k]exp(+j2pi kn/N) unless a comparison row explicitly names another normalization. Bin k has omega_k=2pi k/N radians/sample and f_k=k f_s/N hertz only after N and f_s are declared. For signed display, k>N/2 maps to k-N; for even N the k=N/2 Nyquist bin is self-conjugate and must appear once. Real data obey X[N-k]=X*[k]. Zero padding changes DFT sample spacing but not the N-sample rectangular-window main-lobe width; only additional acquired samples lengthen the observation.

image_pool_decision.reason: No image-pool entry is assigned to this lesson or directly evidences its finite-coordinate conventions. The Cooley-Tukey opening page belongs to the next FFT lesson, is primarily text-bearing, has publisher-rights restrictions, and would not teach bins, symmetry, normalization, or zero-padding resolution by looking at it.

shared_conventions.indices: n,k in {0,...,N-1}; records are half-open and contain exactly N samples
shared_conventions.frequency: omega_k=2pi k/N rad/sample; f_k=k f_s/N Hz; signed k_s=k for k<=floor(N/2), otherwise k-N, with even-N Nyquist shown once
shared_conventions.real_symmetry: X[N-k]=X*[k] for k=1,...,N-1; X[0] and even-N X[N/2] are real
shared_conventions.circular_convolution: Y[k]=X[k]H[k] corresponds to y[n]=sum_{m=0}^{N-1}x[m]h[(n-m) mod N], not unpadded linear convolution

figures.brief_visual: Continuous DTFT curve sampled at N DFT-bin locations
figures.decision: keep as a single raw SVG
figures.tier_reason: One fixed magnitude curve, eight stems, and short axis labels fit a raw SVG; no flowing prose, matrix, or multi-line typeset comparison is needed.
figures.embed: <Figure src="./figures/dtft-dft-bin-samples.svg" alt="The magnitude DTFT of an eight-sample alternating record is a continuous periodic curve, while eight equally spaced DFT stems sample it and leave only bin four at magnitude eight." caption="The DFT does not replace the DTFT curve; it samples one period at N declared coordinates." />
figures.teaching_claim: For a length-N record, X[k] is the record DTFT evaluated at omega_k=2pi k/N; the physical hertz label additionally requires f_s.

exact_data.record: N=8, x[n]=(-1)^n for n=0,...,7 and zero outside the record
exact_data.display: plot |X_8(e^{j omega})| on 0<=omega<2pi and repeat faintly at the two boundaries only to communicate periodicity
exact_data.dft_values: X=[0,0,0,0,8,0,0,0] under the unscaled forward convention
exact_data.physical_example: if f_s=8 kHz, the unsigned labels are 0,1,...,7 kHz and the signed labels are 0,+1,+2,+3,-4,-3,-2,-1 kHz

figures.composition: Use viewBox 0 0 640 330. The amber continuous magnitude curve spans a normalized omega axis; blue stems and filled dots mark the eight DFT samples. Put k=0,...,7 immediately below the dots and a second compact ledger below the plot for omega_k and, conditionally, f_k. Highlight k=4 with a direct X[4]=8 label. A faint continuation at both ends says 2pi periodic without adding a second curve.
required_labels: f_k=k f_s/N only after f_s is known

color_roles.currentColor: axes, bin labels, exact-value annotation, and periodic guides

figures.mobile_and_theme: At 360 px retain all eight stems, k labels, 0/pi/2pi ticks, and the k=4 value; remove minor grid lines before reducing type below 11 viewBox units. Use currentColor and opacity with no baked background.
render_acceptance: Every blue dot lies on the amber curve.
Only k=4 is nonzero and its plotted magnitude is exactly 8.
The horizontal axis is radians/sample; the optional hertz ledger declares f_s=8 kHz rather than treating k as hertz.
The 0 and 2pi endpoints are presented as the same periodic coordinate, not two independent bins.

figures.brief_visual: DFT as correlations against rows of a complex basis matrix
figures.decision: keep as a single component figure
figures.tier_reason: A literal complex-valued matrix, highlighted row, vector cells, and bound KaTeX equations require HTML plus KaTeX around SVG/grid geometry.
figures.embed: <Figure name="DftBasisCorrelations" alt="A four-cell input vector is multiplied by four rows of the complex DFT basis; the highlighted k equals one row computes one times one plus zero times minus j plus minus one times minus one plus zero times j, giving X of one equal to two." caption="Each DFT coefficient is one correlation with a complete complex basis row." />
figures.teaching_claim: The forward DFT is a bank of N exact complex correlations; row k contains exp(-j2pi kn/N) and produces X[k].
figures.composition: Build an aligned left-to-right component: input cells, multiplication arrow, a 4x4 literal basis grid, equality arrow, and output cells. Highlight only row k=1 and output X[1] in the same role color; place the exact scalar correlation below. Use cell outlines and row labels so the matrix remains auditable without color.

color_roles.currentColor: inactive matrix cells, arrows, and row/column indices

figures.mobile_and_theme: Use a desktop horizontal equation and a mobile vertical stack that repeats the multiplication/equality arrows between complete blocks. Keep every cell at least 34 CSS pixels and all complex entries legible at 360 px.
render_acceptance: The k=1 row is [1,-j,-1,j], not the synthesis-sign conjugate.
The dot product yields +2 and the complete output is [0,2,0,2].
Only one row is highlighted, and the same color binds the row label to its formula term.
The component is hook-free, server-rendered, and uses M plus palette constants with no dependencies or Tailwind.

figures.brief_visual: Real-input full spectrum, positive-only spectrum, packed layout, and normalization ledger
figures.decision: keep as a single component figure
figures.tier_reason: The figure maps one coefficient set into three software/reporting layouts and a four-row normalization table; flowing labels and KaTeX are load-bearing.
figures.embed: <Figure name="RealDftConventionLedger" alt="An eight-sample real cosine produces conjugate coefficients of four at bins one and seven; aligned rows map the full two-sided coefficients to signed hertz, a logical packed-real output, a one-sided amplitude of one, and four declared scaling conventions." caption="The same DFT numbers mean different plotted amplitudes and layouts only after the convention is declared." />
figures.teaching_claim: Real-input symmetry removes redundant storage but not negative-frequency meaning, and numerical amplitude is inseparable from the declared forward/inverse normalization and one-sided doubling rule.

exact_data.conjugacy: X[7]=X*[1]=4; X[0] and X[4] are self-conjugate real bins
exact_data.logical_real_output: store X[0],...,X[4]=[0,4,0,0,0] as complex bins and reconstruct X[8-k]=X*[k]; do not imply a universal scalar memory packing
exact_data.one_sided_amplitude: A[1]=2|X[1]|/N=1; use |X[k]|/N without doubling at DC and Nyquist
normalizations: one-sided amplitude from the unscaled DFT: A[1]=1

figures.composition: Use aligned rows with the same eight cell positions: full indices, signed frequencies, unscaled coefficients, conjugate-pair arcs, then a five-cell logical real-output row. Beside or below, show the one-sided amplitude row and normalization ledger. Mark DC and Nyquist as single endpoints; use a brace between k=1 and k=7 rather than duplicating energy.
required_labels: DC and Nyquist: do not double

color_roles.currentColor: zero cells, axes, packing outlines, endpoints, and normalization text

figures.mobile_and_theme: At 360 px stack the full-spectrum map, logical packed row, and ledger; do not horizontally scroll or shrink the eight-bin labels below legibility. Solid/dashed pair arcs and explicit +1/-1 kHz labels carry conjugacy without color.
render_acceptance: The full DFT has magnitude four at both k=1 and k=7 and zero elsewhere.
The one-sided amplitude is one, not four, one-half, or two; DC/Nyquist are explicitly exempt from doubling.
The logical five-complex-bin layout is not mislabeled as a universal library memory format.
The unitary magnitude is sqrt(2), and every alternative scale is named rather than mixed.

figures.brief_visual: Same underlying signal: unpadded, zero-padded, and genuinely longer records
figures.decision: keep as a single component comparison
figures.tier_reason: Three aligned spectra require exact record/padding ledgers and a controlled statement about what changed; HTML plus KaTeX prevents the mini-plots from carrying tiny explanatory text.
figures.embed: <Figure name="PaddingDurationResolution" alt="Three aligned spectra use the same 1024 sample-per-second two-tone signal: a 64-sample DFT is coarse, padding those same 64 samples to 1024 points adds dense samples to the same broad response, and acquiring 256 samples before transforming 1024 points narrows the response and stabilizes separate peaks near 170 and 180 hertz." caption="Padding samples the same finite-record spectrum more densely; more acquired data changes the spectrum's resolving width." />
figures.teaching_claim: Holding the acquired record fixed while increasing transform length refines the frequency grid but cannot create the narrower window response supplied by a longer observation.

exact_data.source: x[n]=cos(2pi 170 n/1024)+0.8cos(2pi 180 n/1024), rectangular window, f_s=1024 Hz
exact_data.panel_1: N=64 acquired samples, L=64 DFT, record aperture N/f_s=62.5 ms, grid Delta f=f_s/L=16 Hz, individual-tone rectangular-window zero-to-zero main-lobe width 2f_s/N=32 Hz
exact_data.panel_2: same first N=64 acquired samples followed by 960 exact zeros, L=1024 DFT, same 62.5 ms aperture and same 32 Hz individual main-lobe width, grid Delta f=1 Hz
exact_data.panel_3: N=256 genuinely acquired samples of the same underlying signal followed by 768 zeros, L=1024 DFT, aperture 250 ms, grid Delta f=1 Hz, individual main-lobe width 8 Hz
exact_data.controlled_comparison: panels 2 and 3 use the same L=1024 and 1 Hz plotted grid; only N and the acquired duration change
exact_data.qualification: main-lobe widths describe each rectangular-windowed tone kernel; the two-tone sum may shift local maxima through interference

figures.composition: Use three near-identical cards with common 140-210 Hz axes and identical vertical normalization. Panel 1 shows sparse DFT stems; panel 2 overlays dense stems on the same broad continuous finite-record curve; panel 3 keeps the dense grid but narrows the two component kernels and marks two peaks. A change ledger beneath the cards has rows for acquired N, transform L, aperture, grid spacing, and main-lobe width, highlighting only the cells that change.

color_roles.accent_amber_#e2903a: 170 Hz component and the changed quantity in each step
color_roles.currentColor: sample stems, shared axes, combined magnitude, and unchanged ledger cells

figures.mobile_and_theme: At 360 px stack all three complete cards in reading order and repeat the 140/170/180/210 Hz ticks. Preserve a common horizontal frequency scale within every card and direct labels for N, L, and aperture.
render_acceptance: Panels 1 and 2 are generated from byte-identical 64 acquired samples; only appended zeros and DFT grid change.
Panels 2 and 3 share L=1024 and a 1 Hz grid, isolating the effect of acquired duration.
The 64-sample continuous finite-record curve does not narrow after padding.
The figure says the longer record resolves this constructed pair; it does not claim zero padding adds information.

nonvisual_contracts_for_writer: State circular convolution separately: DFT-domain multiplication gives y[n]=sum_{m=0}^{N-1}x[m]h[(n-m) mod N]. Linear convolution requires enough zero padding to at least L_x+L_h-1 before the DFT product.
Keep the half-open record n=0,...,N-1 distinct from a claim that the observed signal is periodic; periodic extension is the DFT's coordinate model.
Place PaddingVsDataLab before PaddingDurationResolution so the static comparison summarizes a task the learner has already performed rather than duplicating it decoratively.
